chapter: Race, critics and the big bands
title: White hopes and Miles's band: making room for white stars
summary: Sam believes writers had to move black bands aside to make room for Mulligan, Chet Baker and Getz, and says Miles's band blocked it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I have to talk about the laymen men because he's the man that takes care of us, you know. So these writers started writing about these freedom players, you see. And yeah, I do believe that it was a conspiracy and that because in order for the white musician to get a play, they had to get all these people off the scene man because there wasn't too much places for white musicians to play. Who did you have? Gerry Mulligan, the Superstars, at that time that boy played the trumpet.

Chet Baker and he was a great white hope, singing and playing the trumpet. You got your great Stan Getz. He was your next great white hope, you see. People like Zoot Sims, you know he was mentioned but he wasn't a big star like those guys was, you know. Who else? Like I say, you can count those guys, those white guys on your one hand. Those were your big white superstars in jazz, Bob Brookmeyer, he was mentioned but he wasn't a superstar.

Jim Hall. See but he was playing with a black man. He was playing in Sonny Rollins' band. So that's how he got his name, by playing with Sonny Rollins, you see. He was a fine guitar player but he wasn't that fine, at the time, you see. So they had to write about those people so they could make room for these Superstars to play out here man. You're talking too much about the Messengers. You're talking too much about the great Miles Davis. See Miles Davis had everything sewed up, you know. His band was a rare type. There was no way in the world you could pass him. You couldn't mention nobody else, man, because that band that he had ever since he organized it, it's rough stuff in there boy, you know.
When you get by - so you can't get by the.....
Yeah, it was hitting awful hard. Hard to bypass him.
Yeah see. And so Miles with his attitude and the white up there in the office. He didn't like that too tough.

And the whites all over the country didn't like that too much. Too many people going to hear this little black boy and his trumpet, his band. Can't get in the joint. Concerts is sold out, you see. The white is checking this stuff out. So they write about it, man. They write about this shit, you know. So Miles' new album is nothing too exceptional. It's almost like the last album he made and so on and so on and so on. But Stan Getz is going to come with so and so playing in the band and so, so and so. And he's playing and oh he's fantastic, you know. The man that stoned junkie, you know what I mean, and ain't playing good but he's great and the great white father, man. Well you know they've got to always make room for the white players, you know.
